hero.slide1Body: A professional workspace to structure what your game should become — without silent AI rewrites of your data.
hero.slide2Body: Project Areas become Focus Space folders so systems, story, and content stay navigable as the project grows.
hero.slide3Body: Design Focuses capture target importance separately from structure — criteria you can inspect, not folders you bury ideas in.
hero.slide4Title: Your wording stays the source of truth
hero.slide4Body: Capture the experience you want players to feel. Later analysis and suggestions remain advisory until you accept them.
hero.slide5Body: Link mechanics, characters, quests, and systems so dependencies and design pressure are visible — not buried in notes.
hero.slide6Body: Chat against project context for suggestions and checks. Project Brain never silently mutates your structure or intent.

setup.whatType: What type of project are you creating?
setup.intro: Your stated intention remains the source of truth. Project Brain helps you structure and inspect design decisions — it never silently changes your data. No project is created until you continue to setup.
setup.generalInfo: General setup covers Intent, Project Areas, and Design Focus. Genre templates and game-specific balance tools stay on {game} projects.
setup.createFailed: Could not create the project. Sign in and try again.
setup.leaveMessage: Your type and name selections will be lost.
setup.typeGameDesc: Interactive games with design focus, balance, and systems thinking.
setup.typeCreativeDesc: Narrative, film, art, or other creative work.
setup.typeOtherDesc: Anything that does not fit the categories above.
setup.typeCustomDesc: Define your own project type label.

wizard.introProject: Intent first, then Project Areas and Design Focus. Suggestions are advisory — accept, edit, or reject before anything is saved. Genre templates stay on Game projects.
wizard.introGame: Intent first, then genres, Project Areas, and Design Focus. Suggestions are advisory — accept, edit, or reject before anything is saved.
wizard.prefilled: Pre-filled below for edit — nothing is committed until Finish setup.
wizard.intentHelpProject: Tell the story of what this project should become — the foundation. Your wording is the source of truth. We'll suggest Project Areas and Design Focus sliders from it; you decide what to keep.
wizard.intentHelpGame: Tell the story of the experience you want players to feel. Your wording is the source of truth. We'll suggest genres, Project Areas, and Design Focus sliders from it; you decide what to keep.
wizard.intentPlaceholderProject:
Example:
Build a calm personal finance app that helps people feel in control of irregular income — clear cash-flow views, gentle reminders, and no shamey “you overspent” tone. Optimize for trust, clarity, and low cognitive load. Avoid dark patterns, aggressive upsells, and noisy dashboards.
wizard.intentPlaceholderGame:
Example:
A quiet exploration game about restoring a flooded coastal town. Players rebuild trust with locals through small favors and careful observation — not combat. Optimize for atmosphere, discovery, and emotional payoff. Avoid loot grind and explicit skill trees.
wizard.needIntentProject: Describe what this project should become first.
wizard.needIntentGame: Describe the experience you want to create first.
wizard.areasHelp: What sections do you want to organize this project around? These become top-level folders in Project Structure (Focus Space). No importance sliders — areas are where ideas live, not what the project emphasizes.
wizard.areasHelpGame: What sections do you want to organize this game around? These become top-level folders in Project Structure. No importance sliders — areas are where ideas live, not what the game emphasizes.
wizard.focusHelp: What should this project emphasize? Design Focuses are analysis criteria with target importance — not Project Structure folders. Adjust freely; values are independent and need not sum to 100.
wizard.focusHelpGame: What should this game emphasize? Design Focuses are analysis criteria with target importance — not Project Structure folders. Adjust freely; values are independent and need not sum to 100.
wizard.importanceHint: Higher means more of the experience should optimize for this design pillar.
wizard.reviewAreasHint: Structural folders in Focus Space — no importance.
wizard.reviewFocusesHint: Emphasis criteria with target importance — separate from structure.
wizard.leaveDiscardProgress: Discard draft project “{name}” and return home? Setup progress will be lost and the draft will be deleted.
wizard.leaveDiscardDraft: Leave setup and delete draft project “{name}”?

designFocus.title: Design Focus
designFocus.intro: Target importance forms a points pool. Only Ready nodes with content (≥{minChars} chars) fill that pool via their classifications; empty Ready/Idea stubs add 0. Colors use existing balance thresholds (≤5 green, ≤10 orange, >10 red) on normalized distribution.
designFocus.poolMeta: sum of targetImportance at this level · {percent}% filled by Ready content
designFocus.poolOk: Target pool filled and distribution within thresholds.
designFocus.listMeta: target {target} pts ({share}% of pool) · filled {raw} / {target} · {ready} Ready with content
designFocus.noFillSources: No Ready nodes with enough content (≥{minChars} chars) contribute here.
designFocus.alertEmpty: No Ready nodes with meaningful content yet — target pool is {pool} points.
designFocus.alertUnderfilled: Target pool not filled: {filled} / {pool} points ({remaining} remaining).
designFocus.alertDistribution: Distribution is off ({red} red, {orange} orange) vs Design Focus targets.

balance.title: Balance
balance.intro: Actual vs normalized target at every Design Focus level. Color is from code thresholds (≤5 green, ≤10 orange, >10 red). Confidence is separate.
balance.empty: No design focuses yet. Complete setup or add focuses first.
balance.aiIntro: Narrates code-computed balance. Suggestions never auto-apply.
balance.openIntelligenceSuffix: for direction checks and full analysis.
